title: Smooth constant-coefficient assertions imply open-immersion lower-shriek assertions
statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], r a prime, and R = ULift(Z/rZ). Assume that for every smooth separated finite-type curve g:C → Spec k of dimension at most one [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], the constant R-module sheaf with value R/(r) [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] satisfies all eight assertions [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions]. Then for every smooth curve f:X → Spec k with the same conventions and every open immersion j:U → X [def-weil-open-immersion], j_! of the constant R-module sheaf with value R/(r) on U satisfies all eight assertions on X [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. Empty, disconnected and zero-dimensional curves are allowed.

source.place: Lemma 59.83.7, proof: disjoint smooth components, empty or dense intersection, and dense-open localization

proof.text: Apply H to the ambient smooth curve X. Smoothness makes the local rings regular, hence reduced, and finite type gives local Noetherianity; infer IsReduced X from the reduced stalks. Put R = ULift(ZMod r) and F = constantModSheaf R X r. Its value R/(r) is a finitely generated R-module, so the existing constant-sheaf finite-locally-constant instance and the trivial stratification give constructibility. Applying the additive constantSheaf functor to r times the identity of its value shows r times the identity of F is zero (r = 0 in R).

Let V be the open image of j and E the open complement of closure(V). They are disjoint by V subset closure(V). Their union is the coborder of V and is dense, by Mathlib dense_coborder. Explicitly enumerate these two opens by Fin 2. Apply assertions_iff_dense_open_prime to F and this dense union, using H f, to obtain assertions for extension by zero of the restriction to the union.

Apply assertions_iff_disjoint_open_prime to the two disjoint opens, with the same constructible r-annihilated constant sheaf. Evaluate the resulting family of assertions at index zero to obtain Assertions for V_! V^* F. The disjoint-open equivalence already handles conditional primary and invertible torsion hypotheses.

Use upperStarConstantSheafIso to identify V^* F with constantModSheaf R V r. The canonical open-immersion image isomorphism e:U ≅ V satisfies e.inv followed by j = V.ι. Composition of extension by zero identifies V_! with e.inv_! followed by j_!. For an isomorphism, e.inv_! is naturally isomorphic to e.hom^*. Pullback of the constant sheaf along e.hom gives the constant sheaf on U. Compose these isomorphisms to obtain V_! V^* F ≅ j_! constantModSheaf R U r.

The restriction V^* F is constructible by constructible pullback. X is Noetherian, so V.ι is quasi-compact. Use the open-closed constructibility theorem with V.closedComplement to show V_! V^* F constructible, and transport constructibility through the displayed sheaf isomorphism. Apply assertions_of_underlying_abelian_iso to the image of this isomorphism under the forgetful sheaf functor. This existing public theorem transports all eight assertions; no duplicate cohomology or assertion transport helpers are needed. Empty opens, empty schemes and zero-dimensional schemes are included.

lean.statement:
theorem smoothConstantLowerShriekAssertions_of_constant
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (r : ℕ) [Fact r.Prime]
    (H : ∀ {C : Scheme.{u}} (g : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve g] [Smooth g],
      IsCurve.Assertions (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod r)) g
        (Etale.constantModSheaf (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod r)) C r))
    {X U : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve f] [Smooth f]
    (j : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j] :
    IsCurve.Assertions (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod r)) f
      ((Etale.openImmersionLowerShriek
        (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod r))) j).obj
        (Etale.constantModSheaf (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod r)) U r))
